quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #11
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 28

questions.question: You want to turn left at an upcoming corner. You must yield to:

options.text: Pedestrians on the sidewalk waiting for the walk signal.

questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to pedestrians, cyclists, and vehicles that have a green light.

questions.question: A truck or bus is turning right and you also need to turn right. You should:

options.text: Turn quickly before the truck or bus.
Wait until the truck or bus finishes turning.
Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the truck or bus finishes turning.
questions.explanation: Do not drive between a turning truck or bus and the curb. You could crash. Wait until the truck or bus completes its turn before you turn.

questions.question: Work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs are used to:

options.text: Make drivers frustrated about slow traffic.
Keep traffic away from dangerous work areas.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep traffic away from dangerous work areas.
questions.explanation: Work zones are dangerous for workers and drivers. Watch for cones, barrels, signs, large vehicles, and workers in bright vests.

questions.question: Your car is skidding out of control. You should:
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, do not brake. Steer to regain control until the vehicle moves safely again.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should use your high beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect back and reduce visibility.

questions.question: This red and white sign means you should:

options.text: Stop and look both ways before going.
Let traffic on the road you are entering or crossing go first.
Keep your speed and check for traffic from all directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let traffic on the road you are entering or crossing go first.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means slow down and be ready to stop if needed. Let vehicles, cyclists, and pedestrians pass first. You do not have the right-of-way.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black marks. They alert you to hazards ahead. This sign tells you to prepare for traffic merging from the right.

questions.question: This sign indicates a:
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black marks warn of hazards. Round signs warn about railroad crossings.

questions.question: Which road is most likely to be slippery in cold weather after snow or rain?

options.text: A road in a shaded area

questions.correctAnswerText: A road in a shaded area
questions.explanation: Shaded roads freeze before other areas and thaw out later. They are often icy on cold, wet days.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Cars in the right lane must slow down.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black marks. This sign means traffic may merge from the right. Be ready to let them in safely.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell drivers about dangers ahead. This sign warns you that an intersection is coming so you can prepare to stop or turn.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and do not use your brakes.
Slow down; road is slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down; road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead becomes slippery when it is wet.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A yellow triangle sign with black letters means no passing zone. It appears on the left side of two-lane roads where you cannot pass other vehicles.

questions.question: When a bicyclist is turning left, what can they do?

options.text: They may use the left lane.
They may cut through all lanes.
They may wait on the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may use the left lane.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists ride on the road with traffic. A bicyclist may use the left lane when making a left turn, just like cars do.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires ride on water instead of the road. How do you prevent it in wet weather?

options.text: Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Slow down when the pavement is wet to prevent hydroplaning.

questions.question: What type of sign is this?
questions.explanation: A downward-pointing triangle is always a yield sign. When you see this sign, be ready to slow down or stop.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road winds with turns and curves.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you to be careful when it is wet because the road will be slippery and harder to drive on safely.

questions.question: You are parking downhill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: When parking downhill on any road, turn your wheels toward the edge of the road. This way, if the brakes fail, your car will roll away from traffic, not into it.

questions.question: How do you avoid hydroplaning in rainy conditions?

options.text: Apply brakes as soon as your car starts to skid.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast in wet conditions and your tires lose grip on the road. The best way to prevent it is to drive slower in rain or wet weather than you would in good conditions.

questions.question: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in an unmarked crosswalk. True or false?
questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians in unmarked crosswalks on your side of the road when there are no traffic signals.

questions.question: At a red light with a green arrow, when can you go in the direction of the arrow?

options.text: After you come to a complete stop.
When the light changes to green.
When you are in the correct lane and the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are in the correct lane and the road is clear.
questions.explanation: If you are in a lane with a green arrow signal, you may go in the direction of the arrow when the road is clear. This is true whether the arrow appears alone or with another signal.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers about traffic laws they must follow. This sign means you cannot make a U-turn.

questions.question: When you see this sign, you should stop and do what?

options.text: Check for vehicles only in the direction you plan to go, then proceed.
Let all vehicles that arrive before or after you go first.
Check for traffic in all directions before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for traffic in all directions before proceeding.
questions.explanation: At a stop sign, you must come to a complete stop and look for traffic in all directions before you go.

questions.question: If a driver sees pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead, what should the driver do?

options.text: Continue ahead. The driver has the right-of-way.
Wait for the pedestrians to cross.
Drive around the pedestrians to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the pedestrians to cross.
questions.explanation: Drivers must let pedestrians cross at a crosswalk. You should wait until the crosswalk is clear before you go.

questions.question: You are approaching a red light turning yellow and you have not entered the intersection yet. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get through before the red light.
Slow down and carefully go through the intersection.

questions.explanation: A yellow light tells you to get ready to stop. If you have not entered the intersection, you should try to stop. If you are already in the intersection, leave as quickly as possible.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Drive faster to reach your destination sooner.
Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.
questions.explanation: Watch for signs of being too tired to drive. These include struggling to keep your eyes open, drifting out of your lane, or turning up the radio to stay awake. If you notice these signs, find a safe place to park and rest.

questions.question: Can drivers pass on a two-lane road marked with a single solid yellow line on their side?
questions.explanation: When there is a solid yellow line on your side of the center, you cannot pass. You can only pass when the broken yellow line is nearest to your lane.

questions.question: You park facing uphill where there is no curb. Set the parking brake and turn your wheels which way?

options.text: Toward the edge of the road.
Away from the edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the edge of the road.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill on a road without a curb, turn your wheels toward the right edge of the road. This helps keep your car on the road if the brakes fail.

questions.question: What type of sign is this?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert you to hazards or changes ahead, such as a curve, steep downgrade, or other dangerous situations.

questions.question: What does this sign tell you?

options.text: There is a steep hill ahead.
No trucks are allowed on the upcoming hill.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a steep hill ahead.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign alerts drivers to an upcoming steep hill. Slow down and be ready to control your speed and protect your brakes.

questions.question: If you are arrested with a blood-alcohol concentration of 0.08 percent or higher, your driving privileges will be suspended for at least six months.
questions.explanation: A blood-alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08 percent or higher results in a six-month suspension of your driving privileges.

questions.question: A large truck ahead of you is turning right onto a street with two lanes in each direction. The truck:

options.text: May complete its turn in either of the two lanes.
May have to swing wide to complete the right turn.
Must stay in the right lane at all times while turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: May have to swing wide to complete the right turn.
questions.explanation: When turning, the rear wheels follow a shorter path than the front wheels. Long trucks need more space, so they often swing wide to complete a right turn.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep downhill slope is ahead. Check your brakes before descending.

questions.question: You may pass on a two-lane two-way road within 100 feet of an intersection or railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: You cannot pass on a two-lane two-way road within 100 feet of an intersection or railroad crossing.

questions.question: This white sign means:

options.text: The railroad crossing is controlled. Continue at your regular speed.
Look, listen, and prepare to stop at the crossing if necessary.
Stop at the railroad tracks and wait for a signal before crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, and prepare to stop at the crossing if necessary.
questions.explanation: When approaching a railroad crossing, look and listen for trains. Slow down and be ready to stop. Wait for any trains to pass before you continue.
